idiom_name: epoll/select event loop plus a bounded pthread worker pool joined by a mutex/condvar queue
implementation_notes: There is no runtime to lean on: the asynchronous layer is an epoll (or kqueue/select) loop that must never block, the queueing layer is a hand-rolled bounded buffer guarded by a mutex and two condition variables, and the synchronous layer is a fixed pool of pthreads that wait for work and run the blocking service routine. The classic structure is fully justified here because the platform gives no alternative, so the design decisions are pool size, queue bound and the overflow policy of the enqueue path.
pitfalls: Any blocking call inside the reactor thread - a read, a lock held by workers, a slow decode - collapses the two layers back into one and serialises all connections.
Threads waiting in pthread_cond_wait must re-test the queue predicate in a while loop; a bare if turns a spurious or stolen wake-up into lost work.
An unbounded queue hides overload: size the buffer and decide what queue_push does when it is full.
Worker exit paths that forget pthread_mutex_unlock or the condvar signal leave the reactor blocked or the queue permanently full.
